reports.sourceQuestion: Compute exact sums of batches of signed integer measurements before we consider optimizations. Some batches are empty, some contain one value, and others are much larger. Values can be positive or negative. Explain how you would validate an implementation and return useful error information. There is an essential final condition: use signed sixty-four-bit output, detect overflow, and reject an overflowing batch rather than wrapping or returning a partial sum.

reports.answer: I’m interpreting “signs sixty four bit output” as signed 64-bit output. Compute each batch’s exact sum with an arbitrary-precision accumulator, then reject the batch if its final sum is outside −2^63 through 2^63−1; intermediate excursions can cancel, so they alone should not cause rejection. Validate empty batches returning zero, single values, mixed signs, large batches, both boundaries, sums just outside them, and intermediate overflow followed by cancellation, comparing against an independent exact reference. Return either the complete sum or a structured error with the batch index and an overflow code—never a wrapped value or partial sum; invalid measurements should also identify their position.
